findings.title: ANY() bound to a JS array will not produce a valid Postgres array predicate
findings.body: Team and org authorization now emit `"teamId" = ANY(${teamIds})` and `"userId" = ANY(${userIds})` (also at the team-scope builder around line 201). Prisma.sql does not turn a JavaScript number[] into a PostgreSQL array parameter; the array is either expanded into multiple placeholders (`ANY($1, $2, ...)`, a syntax error) or bound as text/json, which fails at runtime with an operator/type error such as `integer = text` or `op ANY/ALL (array) requires array on right side`. Those are the only predicates that restrict team and org insights, so team/org queries throw or cannot be applied. Use `IN (${Prisma.join(ids)})` (already guarded against empty lists) or an explicitly cast single array parameter, and run the resulting SQL against Postgres.

findings.title: findMany removed, so authorization is no longer applied at the query boundary
findings.body: The public `findMany` method, which always merged authorization and filter conditions into `bookingTimeStatusDenormalized.findMany`, was replaced by `getBaseConditions()` returning a SQL fragment. No other file in this PR updates callers. Any existing caller of `findMany` will fail to compile, and authorization is now optional: a caller that queries `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` without interpolating this fragment reads rows with no scope check. The old method also merged caller `where` (dates, status, select). `getBaseConditions` cannot express that, and because a `Prisma.Sql` object is always truthy the trailing branches that return only filters or `1=0` are dead—the fragment is easy to misuse and nothing in the service still enforces it.

findings.title: Team and org SQL is never executed, so broken ANY() predicates still pass
findings.body: Authorization tests only deep-equal `Prisma.Sql` objects against another `Prisma.sql` template that uses the same `ANY(${array})` construction. That comparison checks string/value shape, not that Postgres accepts the query. The only `$queryRaw` (around line 481) is user scope (`userId = $1 AND teamId IS NULL`) and never hits `= ANY(...)`. A syntax or type error in the team/org authorization SQL therefore ships with a green suite. Execute those fragments against `BookingTimeStatusDenormalized` for owner, admin, member, empty team, and a team that is not a child of the org.
